correctness.rationale: The pulse product and between-pulse growth yield the exact periodic, positive factor S. Independent reduction: V(t)=S(t)x(t)^λ/y(t), using the periodic right-continuous S, is continuous at every pulse, and V'=gSx^λ between pulses by cancellation. Positivity, logistic bounds and finitely many fixed positive multipliers give global solutions and uniformly bounded intra-cycle logarithmic drifts. If V remained bounded, integrability of gSx^λ and those drift bounds would force x→0 uniformly by phase, and y=Sx^λ/V→0 as well. But then the log of x increases by a uniformly positive amount per sufficiently late cycle, since the net resident growth log P+∫r>0, a contradiction. Thus V→∞ and y→0 by bounded x. The perturbed affine reciprocal period map for x has limiting slope (P exp(∫r))^-1<1 and the resident fixed point; it gives x→x_* uniformly in phase with the specified pulse convention. Increments V((n+1)T)−V(nT) converge to I=∫gSx_*^λ>0, so V(nT)/n→I, yielding the phase limit. Since (log V)'=gy with no jumps, J_n=log(V((n+1)T)/V(nT)), hence nJ_n→1 and ∫_0^{NT}gy=log(V(NT)/V(0))=log N+log(y(0)I/x(0)^λ)+o(1). This proves the limits with arbitrary strictly positive initial values, all phases, and zero-size pulses allowed. The example script integrates a finite sample and was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: The constant 1 is for the dimensionless g-weighted cycle load, not the unweighted invader density; exact neutrality, alignment, positive gap and positive initial populations matter.

value.rationale: The exact boundary between strict invasion cases is a motivated quantitative gap. A globally valid phase profile identifies how a neutral competitor vanishes despite a unit linear invasion multiplier; the universal normalized load and explicit initial-state offset translate that profile into measurable model quantities. The value is the combined result for an aligned seasonal and impulsive family, not novelty of ratio cancellation alone.
residual_risks: Deterministic model, not a prediction of stochastic extinction time or a generic neutral competitive-system classification.
